The Chicago, Illinois-based pharma giant recorded $17.4B in revenue for the quarter, with ~10% YoY growth beating the consensus by $50M as sales from Skyrizi and Rinvoq climbed 23% and 24% YoY, respectively, to $5.8B and $2.7B.

However, the company’s total immunology sales only grew ~16% YoY to $9.2B as Humira, whose U.S. market exclusivity expired in 2023, added $683M with a 31% YoY decline amid biosimilar competition still exceeding $679M, projected by analysts, according to Bloomberg data.

The company recorded $3.4B in sales from its Neuroscience portfolio, with Botox therapeutic and Vraylar antipsychotic therapy generating roughly $1.1B each, up ~10% and ~14% YoY, respectively, exceeding the consensus of $1.07B and $ 1.06 B.
Oncology franchise, meanwhile, added roughly $5.0B in net sales as lymphoma drugs, Venclexta and Imbruvica, generated $2.3B and $1.6B, with 13% YoY growth and a ~27% YoY decline, respectively.

During the quarter, the company’s gross and operating margins improved to 85.1% and 48.7% from 83.9% and 30.9% in the prior-year period, while its non-GAAP earnings per share more than doubled to $3.82 on a non-GAAP basis, exceeding the consensus by $0.05
